researcher_notes: Phillips 66 Freeport LPG Export Terminal (Freeport, TX) declared fully operational in December 2016; first contracted cargo departed on the VLGC 'Commander' on Dec 16, 2016. Year = 2016 (commercial start). Phillips 66 IR is the primary source; OGJ, Hydrocarbon Engineering and Gas Processing & LNG are independent trade-press confirmations. All four verified PASS for '2016'+'Freeport'.

Targa Resources' Galena Park international LPG export terminal (Houston Ship Channel) brought its international LPG export expansion online in two phases: Phase I in 3Q 2013 and Phase II in 3Q 2014. Year = 2013 for the start of large-scale international LPG export service. Only one source (Targa's own Jan-2013 press release) verified PASS for '2013'+'Galena Park' before the session web limit; it announces the project coming online in 3Q2013. CAVEAT: the underlying marine terminal pre-dated 2013, so 2013 is the international-LPG-export online year rather than the terminal's original commissioning; a reviewer may want to confirm GEM's intended milestone. Independent corroboration (Argus: 'Phase I completed September 2013') seen in research but not verifiable (bot-blocked).

Golden Pass import terminal (Sabine Pass, TX; QatarEnergy/ExxonMobil) was completed 2009-2010 and received its first LNG cargo Oct 2010, then sat idle as the shale glut killed US import demand; multiple sources describe it as dormant 'for almost 3 years' as of 2014, implying idling from ~2011. Likely mothball year = 2011, BUT the only explicit '2011' attribution traces to GEM (non-citable/circular), and I could not verify an independent non-GEM page tying '2011' to the mothballing before the session web limit. Left UNRESOLVED; reviewer could confirm via EIA Golden Pass import-volume data (imports ceasing after 2011).

Harvest Midway Terminal (crude storage/pumping hub at Taft, TX, feeding the Ingleside export terminals near Corpus Christi) was announced Nov 2019 with the Midway Terminal projected in-service at the start of 4Q 2020. Harvest's own history page states 'In 2020, Harvest completed the Ingleside Pipeline... transports products from our Midway Terminal.' Year = 2020. Both verified URLs are Harvest's own (one origin) -> single primary source, tier medium; no independent media source confirming the 2020 in-service date was verifiable before the session web limit.

Houston Fuel Oil Terminal Company (HFOTCO), Houston Ship Channel, was founded in 1978, originally dedicated to storing/blending/moving residual fuel oil (added crude oil handling in the early 1990s). Year = 1978 (founding used as operating-start proxy). One industry source (TankTerminals) verified PASS for '1978'+'Houston Fuel Oil Terminal'; RBN Energy independently states 'Founded in 1978' but was bot-blocked (403) and could not be verified. Tier medium pending a second verifiable source.

IMTT St. Rose (St. Charles Parish, LA; International-Matex Tank Terminals) operating-start year is ambiguous: the site has operated as an oil/export terminal since 1922 (Cities Service Terminal Co., per St. Charles Parish history), with IMTT (founded 1939 at Avondale) taking over in later years; GEM's intended 'operating' milestone year is unclear and no clean, independently verifiable year was confirmed before the session web limit. Left UNRESOLVED; reviewer should decide whether the milestone is the 1922 terminal origin or IMTT's acquisition year.

The proposal to convert the Kenai LNG terminal (Nikiski, AK) into an LNG import facility ('Kenai LNG Cool Down Project') was filed with FERC on March 29, 2019 by Marathon subsidiary Trans-Foreland Pipeline Co. (docket CP19-118); FERC issued its environmental-review schedule notice June 2019 and approved the project Dec 17, 2020. Year proposed = 2019. Primary/regulatory source (Federal Register, June 2019 notice) + independent media (Petroleum News) both verified PASS for '2019'+'Kenai'.

Lake Charles LNG export (liquefaction) project, Trains 1-3 (Trunkline/Southern Union -> Energy Transfer + BG Group, later Shell). Strong unverified lead: the export project was publicly advanced ~2013 (Energy Transfer 'decision in 2013 to add liquefaction'; DOE non-FTA export authorization May 2013), though an earlier DOE FTA export application dates to ~2011. Could not lock a verified URL for a specific proposed year before the session web limit (Wikipedia page lacked the '2013' token at the cited anchor; NS Energy was bot-blocked). Left UNRESOLVED; likely year is 2013 (or 2011 if GEM counts the first DOE export filing) — quick reviewer confirmation needed.

Lake Charles / Trunkline LNG import terminal (Lake Charles, LA) began importing in 1982; import demand collapsed with the US shale glut around 2010-2011 (DOE FTA export approval came in 2011, signaling the pivot away from imports), but the terminal retained regasification capability for years and no source pins a discrete mothball year. No independently verifiable year for the mothballed milestone was obtained before the session web limit. Left UNRESOLVED; candidate window ~2011-2012, reviewer could confirm via EIA Lake Charles import-volume data.

Seabrook Logistics LLC (Magellan Midstream/LBC 50-50 JV) crude-oil and condensate marine terminal near Seabrook, TX (Galveston Bay). The Dec-2016 Magellan/LBC joint announcement states the new storage and pipeline infrastructure was expected to be operational in the first quarter of 2017. Year = 2017 (announced/projected commercial start). Only the Magellan/LBC press release (one origin; reprints are the same wire story) verified PASS for '2017'+'Seabrook'; tier medium. CAVEAT: 2017 is the projected start from the Dec-2016 release; no independent post-startup confirmation of the actual 2017 in-service date was verifiable before the session web limit.
